dialogue.speaker: Sergeant Hollis
lines: Fair morning -- such as it is. Sergeant Hollis. The storm took our lights twice last night and took Mr. Vesper once, all told.
The coroner's man wrote 'heart.' Mr. Pell pays better than grief, and he says your eyes are for hire. So: look.
The household's five guests are still under this roof, dry and quiet and telling tidy stories. I've written their stories into your case file.

dialogue.speaker: Sergeant Hollis
lines: Five of them slept here: the niece Peggy, the agent Ashcombe, the doctor Marsh, the apprentice Grimm, and Colette, who cooks and keeps the ledger.
Their stories are tidy. Tidy is what I'd watch, if I were you. The notebook has them all -- People tab.

dialogue.speaker: Sergeant Hollis
lines: Start in the hall. It keeps the night's clockwork: who came, who went, and what stopped when the storm did.
When the hall has told you its story, say it to the parlour door. That door opens for arithmetic, not for keys.

dialogue.speaker: Sergeant Hollis
lines: The house is yours, detective. Mind the rug in the parlour -- it remembers feet.

dialogue.speaker: Sergeant Hollis
lines: Fair enough -- that's the hall read like a hall. I've pulled the tape off the parlour door.
Mind the rug. It remembers feet.
